proof.text: Choose each ordinary change-of-rings functor, its additive structure, and its universal unbounded left-derived pair from lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings. Exact restriction and normalized ordinary extension/restriction adjunctions come from lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction. The K-flat computation assertion is independent of the choice of adjunction.

The comparison of successive ordinary restrictions with restriction along the composite is the identity on sections (the functors are definitionally equal). Transport the composite ordinary adjunction along this comparison and use uniqueness of left adjoints to define the ordinary extension comparison. Its unit equation identifies its value on 1 tensor (1 tensor x). Outer linearity and semilinearity of the second unit give t tensor (s tensor x) mapping to b(s)t tensor x. Applying the inverse isomorphism gives the stated inverse formula.

Apply lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-hom-comparison to each chosen ordinary adjunction and universal left-derived pair. This chooses derived adjunctions compatible with the ordinary Hom equivalence on every homotopy representative. Taking the identity ordinary map proves the required derived-unit normalization. Derive the composite restriction comparison using the exact-functor mapDerivedCategoryCompIso, then apply uniqueness of left adjoints to obtain the derived extension comparison and its composite-unit equation.

proof.text: Apply the composite derived Hom equivalence to the representative equation. Naturality and the Hom-comparison formula rewrite the iterated extension side as the localization of the iterated ordinary Hom equivalence, followed by the inverses of the restriction factorization isomorphisms. The normalization of the derived restriction composition cancels those factors. The ordinary composite-unit equation, applied degreewise and passed through the homotopy quotient, identifies the remaining ordinary transpose with the direct unit. Adjoint uniqueness identifies the direct side with the same expression. This proves the representative equation on all homotopy objects, hence in particular on the specified K-flat representatives.

proof.text: Apply lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback to identity inverse image with the identity adjunction and structural map a. Its conclusion says that the ordinary first extension of a flat-term K-flat complex is again flat-term K-flat. The second computation is therefore invertible by the computation assertion of lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction. No flatness of either coefficient map is assumed.

Exact-functor derived composition is associative by Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso_assoc. Since the ordinary restriction comparisons are identities, the inverse composition comparisons obey the required restriction coherence. Identify the derived extension comparison with Mathlib Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso and apply leftAdjointCompIso_assoc. This proves the stated threefold extension equality, including its equality transport for the composite ring map.

Expand the coefficient-square comparisons. Use associativity for (alpha,a-prime,b-prime) to combine the final comparison. Associativity for (a,beta,b-prime) cancels the middle inverse comparison. Transport the composition comparisons along the two given equalities of ring maps. Associativity for (a,b,gamma) gives the outer comparison. Equality transports compose and their proofs are irrelevant, so the resulting transport is exactly the one specified by the outer equality hab. These are equalities of natural-transformation components at arbitrary derived objects.

title: Successive derived scalar extensions agree with direct quotient extension
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $R\xrightarrow{a}S\xrightarrow{b}T$ be maps of sheaves of commutative rings, and use their module sheaves and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Derived scalar extension is the K-flat derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For every $C\in D(R)$ there is a canonical natural isomorphism $(C\otimes_R^L S)\otimes_S^L T\cong C\otimes_R^L T$. On a K-flat flat-term representative $K^\bullet$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], this isomorphism is represented by $(K^\bullet\otimes_R S)\otimes_S T\to K^\bullet\otimes_R T$, $(x\otimes s)\otimes t\mapsto x\otimes b(s)t$, with inverse $x\otimes t\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes t$. Under these identifications the composite of the scalar-extension units for $a$ and $b$ is the unit for $ba$ (after restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]). The comparison is natural in $C$ and in the composable ring maps and its iterated comparisons agree. This includes ordinary commutative rings by using the one-object site with only the identity covering.
